speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes, such as whether you seem aware of your surroundings or have a memory of the events?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Sleep Terrors (Night Terrors)

These episodes occur during deep sleep, so the child often does not wake fully or remember them, unlike nightmares which happen later in the night. The fact that she can be consoled quickly and returns to normal the next morning also points away from other conditions. We should still check for any potential triggers like stress or sleep deprivation.
